subject: Business
title: Succession Planning: Preparing Your Replacement
description: A fast breakdown of Succession Planning: Preparing Your Replacement for builders.

hook.text: When Disney CEO Bob Iger retired, his successor lasted two years. Iger had to come back. The succession failed.

buildup.text: Succession planning means developing leaders who can replace you — before you need replacing.

discovery.text: The best successions start years early. GE's Jack Welch spent three years vetting his replacement.

twist.text: Founders often resist succession. They confuse the company's identity with their own.

climax.text: Apple's Tim Cook was groomed for years. The smoothest successions look effortless because of invisible preparation.

punchline.text: A leader who can't be replaced hasn't led well enough.

quiz.question: Why do many founders resist succession planning?
options: They confuse the company's identity with their own
They believe the company will close after they leave
Succession is only needed in public companies

details.summary: Succession planning identifies and develops future leaders to ensure smooth transitions when current leaders depart. The best leaders begin preparing potential successors from day one, viewing talent development as a core leadership responsibility rather than an HR administrative task.
details.whyItMatters: Organizations without succession plans face crisis when key leaders leave unexpectedly. The average CEO tenure is under five years, making succession planning essential for continuity, stability, and long-term organizational health.
takeaways: Begin identifying and developing potential successors from day one in any role
Succession planning is a leadership responsibility, not just an HR process
Smooth transitions preserve organizational knowledge and stakeholder confidence

faq.question: When should succession planning start?
faq.answer: Immediately upon taking a leadership role. Identify high-potential team members early. Provide stretch assignments that develop leadership skills. Create exposure to senior leaders and stakeholders. Document institutional knowledge consistently. Waiting until departure is planned is far too late.

faq.question: Should organizations favor internal or external successors?
faq.answer: Internal successors preserve culture and institutional knowledge while providing continuity. External successors bring fresh perspectives and challenge entrenched thinking.
